_comment: Wingtra WingtraOne GEN II survey drone. A true tailsitter: the whole aircraft stands on its tail to hover and pitches over to fly, and the same two motors do the lifting and the cruising.

_published.source: Wingtra technical specifications, WingtraOne GEN II
_published.battery: two 99 Wh packs, each 4S3P Samsung INR18650-25R, 14.4 V, 604 g

_inferred: Wing area, CD0, Oswald, propeller size and motor electrical parameters are NOT published. Wing area follows from the published 1.25 m span and 0.68 m body depth; the rest are ordinary parts for this class.
_calibration: CD0 back-solved so the model reproduces the published 59 min flight time over a climb/transition/cruise/land profile flown to a 15% reserve. A first-principles guess of 0.024 gave 66.8 min — 13% optimistic, which is what you would expect from a tailsitter's bluff body, exposed motor pods and landing feet. The higher figure is the honest one.
_motor_model_migration: cruise_eff is the PROPELLER's efficiency alone. Before v1.11 the VTOL had no motor electrical model and this field was the combined motor-and-propeller figure (0.70); it was converted by dividing out the motor efficiency the Kv/Rm/I0 model now computes at the cruise point (0.869), so the cruise leg costs what it did before and the motor's loss is now itemised rather than hidden. CD0 was NOT re-tuned. With the motor model the profile flies 58.4 min against the published 59.
